meta.title: Thai A1 Beginner
meta.subtitle: 500 words · both directions, as two cards per word
meta.desc: Both study directions in one deck: Thai → English (see the Thai, recall the meaning) and English → Thai (see an English meaning, recall the Thai). Each direction is a card of its own with its own schedule, so recognising a word and producing it are learnt separately. 500 words for a beginner, aligned to A1 of the Common European Framework of Reference, whose global descriptor begins 'Can understand and use familiar everyday expressions and very basic phrases aimed at the satisfaction of needs of a concrete type' — a learner here is able to introduce themselves and others, to ask and answer questions about personal details such as where they live, people they know and things they have, and to interact in a simple way provided the other person talks slowly and clearly and is prepared to help. WHERE THESE WORDS COME FROM, since it matters: no exam board publishes a graded word list for Thai, so this deck is not any examination's vocabulary and does not claim to be. It is assembled from two things that can be stated. 341 of the 500 come from a vocabulary written for the level's scope — greetings and the polite particles, introducing yourself, family, numbers and the classifiers they are counted with, telling the time, days and months, food and drink, shopping and money, the home, the town and getting about, the body and feeling ill, the weather, colours, and the pronouns, question words, prepositions and conjunctions every sentence is built out of — and the other 159 are the commonest remaining words of Thai, taken from the word counts of the Thai National Corpus, a large collection of written Thai. The cards are dealt by that frequency, so the words you meet most often come first. Every headword is printed in Thai script with a romanisation beneath it in the Paiboon system, which marks the TONE on every syllable — no mark for mid, à low, â falling, á high, ǎ rising — because a Thai word said on the wrong tone is a different word; the Thai Alphabet deck, the first in this collection, teaches the script and the rules that decide a tone. 76 nouns show the classifier they are counted with (a house is counted in หลัง, an animal in ตัว), and there are no forms to learn: Thai words never change shape. Example sentences come with 466 of the 500 words, three apiece for 430 of them, with the word picked out in colour and a speaker beside the sentence and the headword. Sources. Level: the Common European Framework of Reference (Council of Europe), global scale. Meanings, romanisation, classifiers and some example sentences: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Frequency: the Thai National Corpus word list as distributed by PyThaiNLP (CC0). Example sentences: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.
